problems.title: Dynamic minima combine incompatible routes
problems.source_location: Current paper, Section 3.4, p. 6, Appendix B.1, p. 17; author rgfn/gfns/reaction_gfn/dynamic_library/reaction_dynamic_library.py, lines 112–118 and 173–208.
claim: Independent stored minima determine a realizable dynamic fragment route.
analysis: The current on_end_sampling independently minimizes reaction count and cost for each SMILES; retrieve_all_additional_fragments exports the minimum count together with the independently selected cost. Consider two discovered certificates for one intermediate: \((k,c)=(1,100)\) and \((2,10)\), both within the four-reaction budget. These nonnegative costs can arise in the abstract positive-yield model with unit yields. The stored pair becomes \((1,10)\), which neither discovered route realizes. ReactionEnv uses the exported count for tree budgets and PathCostProxy uses the exported cost, so a continuation can inherit a cheap cost requiring a longer subtree while passing with the shorter count. This is an exact invariant failure of the released dynamic-library representation; it is not a claim that a particular real molecule or a known proportion of paper samples has such routes.
result: The dynamic-library representation can destroy the coupling needed for the core cost/feasibility claim. This does not quantify how often published samples use such conflicting routes.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Store one consistent route with its count/cost, or maintain nondominated route certificates and expand them consistently.
problems.impact_rationale: Independent marginal minima produce an impossible joint route certificate, undermining the central dynamically composed cost/feasibility representation itself. This is a structural counterexample, not merely an unbound release-runtime fault.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Backward budgets omit fragment-subtree reactions
problems.source_location: Author reaction_env.py, lines 307–333; policies/cost_biased_backward_policy.py, lines 90–117, and policies/decomposability_guided_backward_policy.py, lines 79–105, under rgfn/gfns/reaction_gfn/.
claim: Backward cost models receive the remaining reaction budget.
analysis: The current environment subtracts the reaction itself and all side-fragment subtree reaction counts. Both current predictor-query branches instead pass state.num_reactions minus one. For product count \(3\) with one side fragment requiring \(1\) reaction, the environment’s precursor count is \(3-1-1=1\), whereas the model query receives \(2\). The discrepancy disappears for original fragments with zero subtree counts. It is a local state-budget mismatch; its effect on published scores is unmeasured.

assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.

problems.title: Cache keys and Boolean writes lose known information
problems.source_location: Author rgfn/gfns/reaction_gfn/policies/guidance_models/cost_models.py, lines 55–80; decomposable_models.py, lines 55–80; proxies/path_cost_proxy.py cache definition.
claim: Cache lookup and override paths use known reachability/cost information consistently.
analysis: The current cost branch now converts Molecule objects to SMILES before querying its string-keyed cache; the old cost-key mismatch is fixed and is not alleged as current. The decomposability branch still tests the unnormalized incoming object keys against a string-keyed dictionary. Even with a string-key cache hit, its chained Boolean assignment modifies an advanced-indexed temporary, rather than the original prediction. Thus a known reachable entry predicted as \(0.1\) remains \(0.1\), instead of being forced to \(1\). Its non-default override branch writes the cached cost itself into the probability: cost \(7\) would produce output \(7\), outside \([0,1]\). These current source defects are separate from historical experiment provenance.

problems.title: The general Bellman recurrence needs monotonicity
claim: The general path-cost recursion can be evaluated using minimum prefixes.
analysis: The current general framework allows transition cost to depend on accumulated prefix cost, then moves the minimum inside that transition. If two prefixes reaching the same state cost \(1\) and \(2\), and the continuation is \(C(x)=(x-2)^2\), the true completed minimum is \(0\), whereas applying the continuation only to the cheapest prefix gives \(1\). All costs are nonnegative. Nondecreasing dependence on prefix cost and a sufficient state restore the finite minimum interchange. The concrete synthesis recurrence \(C^S(x)=(x+c)/y\), with \(y>0\), is strictly increasing and therefore is not refuted by this general-framework counterexample.

problems.title: Tree probability does not identify chemical-space cardinality
claim: The sampled-tree fraction identifies the increase in distinct chemical-space size.
analysis: A sampled nondecomposable fraction \(43\%\) corresponds to a sampled probability ratio \(43/57\simeq75.44\%\). Distinct molecules can have unequal numbers and probabilities of synthesis trees, so that ratio does not imply \(75\%\) more distinct molecules in chemical space.

problems.title: Diagnostic and unused-branch defects are local
problems.source_location: Author guidance_models/decomposable_models.py, lines 151–188 and 205–215; guidance_models/cost_models.py, cost-correlation metric; current paper Appendix A.3.2.
claim: The auxiliary accuracy/correlation measures have the stated definitions.
analysis: The current decomposability predictor applies sigmoid and then computes accuracy using a zero threshold. Since \(\operatorname{sigmoid}(z)>0\) for every finite logit, all such predictions count as positive. Probabilities \((0.1,0.8,0.3,0.9)\) with labels \((0,1,0,1)\) give \(50\%\) under that rule, versus \(100\%\) at threshold \(1/2\). The cost diagnostic still computes Pearson correlation with np.corrcoef while naming it Spearman. The older inverse-cost class with a misspelled attribute is absent from the current guidance_models module and is historical only. Negative examples are capped by the number collected, so the stated negative fraction is a target when supply is insufficient. None of these observations independently establishes that the final mode/scaffold counts are wrong.

problems.title: Mode limits and run manifests remain unresolved
problems.source_location: configs/rgfn_seh_proxy.gin; trainer/metrics/reaction_metrics.py, lines 451-452; official PDF: main mode-count table, Appendix B, Appendix J.2.3/Figure 15, p. 28, and compute-resource checklist, p. 33.
claim: Public mode limits and run configuration explain the reported counts.
analysis: The current sEH configuration still caps modes at \(5000\), and its greedy metric stops at that cap, whereas the paper reports values such as \(37714\). An unrecorded override or offline evaluator could reconcile this; a fabricated-result conclusion does not follow. The greedy, reward-ordered mode set also need not be maximum-cardinality, and its exact similarity boundary needs consistent specification. The paper discloses matched forward-trajectory totals and incomplete resource tracking. Its cost-change experiment continues training without resetting parameters; that does not establish that all networks except the cost predictor were frozen. Per-run configurations, uncertainty units and the exact frozen-parameter policy remain necessary for stronger reconstruction/attribution claims.
result: This is a scope/provenance gap, not proof that the stronger empirical conclusion is false.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Reconcile the specific equation, reported quantity or source contract described above. Corrected full-experiment results remain unverified.
